newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends higher vs dlr as dealers sell.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends higher vs dlr as dealers sell.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed stronger at 35.65/66 per dollar on Thursday against the day's opening of 35.70/72, dealers said.

The rupee opened weaker at 35.70/72 and closed at 35.65/66, while the market was in a selling mood, a dealer said. The premiums on forward dollar were down due to the continuous swap pressure in the money market, he said.

The market saw substantial selling pressure at 35.70 and later it dropped to 35.66 rupees per dollar. The forward premia for April opened at 115-116 paise and subsequently came down to 109 or a 6.25 percent fall, on heavy receiving pressure from the market, a dealer said.
"Pretty dull," a dealer said. "There were a lot of sellers and no major action from state-run banks," a dealer said.
He said the forwards came down, but dealers were still analysing the impacts of the Reserve Bank of India's guidelines permitting banks to lend from their expatriate funds.
